title: On the Category-Theoretic Independence of Meaning, Object, Name and Existence
summary: We prove a category-theoretic independence theorem for four fundamental notions: meaning, object, name, and existence. Working in a Lawvere-style categorical semantics and in particular in toposes, we show that these notions occupy distinct structural levels (object, morphism, element, and internal logical level) and are not uniformly recoverable from one another. The key separation arises between internal existence and global naming.
